text: atom.element symbols: 'c' carbon, 'h' hydrogen, 'o' oxygen, 'n' nitrogen, 's' sulfur, 'cl' chlorine, 'p' phosphorus, 'na' sodium, 'br' bromine, 'f' fluorine, 'i' iodine, 'sn' tin, 'pb' lead, 'te' tellurium, 'ca' calcium.
atom.element also stores rarer lowercase symbols: 'b' boron, 'cu' copper, 'k' potassium, 'si' silicon, 'y' yttrium, 'zn' zinc.
bond.bond_type is '-' for a single bond, '=' for a double bond and '#' for a triple bond.
molecule.label is '+' when the molecule is carcinogenic (cancer-causing) and '-' when it is not carcinogenic.
IDs embed their molecule: atom.atom_id 'TR000_1' is atom 1 of molecule 'TR000'; bond.bond_id 'TR000_1_2' is the bond in 'TR000' between atoms 'TR000_1' and 'TR000_2'.

connected stores every bond twice, once per direction (atom_id and atom_id2 swapped), so the atoms of a bond are exactly the connected.atom_id values for its bond_id; also joining on atom_id2 duplicates them.
"Elements of the toxicology" of a molecule means atom.element of the atoms whose atom.molecule_id is that molecule.
